in_greek.name: Ιεσιάς
in_greek.meaning: Ο Θεός γνωρίζει, ο Θεός αποκαλύπτει
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Ιεσιάς προέρχεται από τις ελληνικές λέξεις που σχετίζονται με την έννοια του Θεού που γνωρίζει ή αποκαλύπτει. Στην παράδοση της Εκκλησίας, το όνομα αυτό συνδέεται με την έννοια της θειας φώτισης και της αποκαλύψεως.

in_latin.name: Iesian
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Iesian derivatur ex Latinis vocibus quae significant 'Deus scit' vel 'Deus revelat'. In traditione Christiana, nomen hoc habet connotationem revelationis divinae et scientiae.

historical_references.reference: The Jesians were a Jewish sect that emerged during the Second Temple period in ancient Israel. They were known for their strict adherence to Jewish law and their belief in the imminent arrival of a divine messiah. The Jesians were mentioned in the New Testament Book of Acts, specifically in Acts 21:20 where Paul was warned not to bring any gentiles into the temple to avoid provoking the Jesians and their allies, the Sadducees.

During the medieval period, the name Jesian was used to refer to a member of the Order of the Jesuits, a Roman Catholic religious order founded in 1540. The Jesuits were known for their rigorous education and their missionary work, particularly in expanding the reach of the Catholic Church in Asia and South America.
